# CHD-3.5 Reader-Artifact QA Report
Delivered artifact: `CHD-3.5-complete-navigable.pdf` SHA-256: `5c8de61683cfa25cfccd49b9c1e0cc169c45bc7814c604770e7f86b46522f743` Pages: 3247 (A4) · bookmarks 1067 · internal links 1214 · PDF page labels Arabic 1..3247. Print variant: `CHD-3.5-complete-print.pdf`, SHA-256 `2806344e020c5b878c5eca9811a801e36c9a49a21702c604c2732f46ef0df2ab`, 3247 pages (94 % scale, 3 % margins). Superseded this round: V05-round artifact `2c2badf1…` (1378 pp); section 21 and 24 were recomposed, the other twenty-five sections are byte-for-byte the same sheet set as that build.
## R35 round 2 — V01 / V02 / V06 closed, V19 gate extended

### R35-V01 (BLOCKING) — schema tables no longer lose visible rows Root causes, all fixed in the generator rather than in the pictured samples:
1. **Character-budget table pagination.** Section 21 tables were split by byte count, which cannot see wrapped row height; sheets therefore promised `ROWS 7–12` and printed three rows before the fixed page box clipped the rest. The packer now paginates section-21 tables by *measured row height* (`render_book._t21_row_mm`: per-column character budget × wrapped-line height + row padding, `BAND_BUDGET_MM = 190`). Continuation placards are computed from the rows actually emitted. 2. **Escaped pipes inside regex cells.** `\|` inside a canonical pattern cell split the markdown row into phantom columns; `table-layout: fixed` then squeezed the real Storage column to one glyph width — the observed vertical single-letter strip. Cells are now split on unescaped pipes only, and the canonical `\|` bytes are printed unchanged. 3. **Angle-bracket identifiers eaten as HTML.** `/chd/acceptance/<objective-id>/<crit-id>` printed as `/chd/acceptance//` because `<objective-id>` parsed as an unknown element. `inline()` now escapes HTML metacharacters before rendering inline code. 4. **Table CSS.** Section 21 has its own fixed column shares for 2–6 column families, `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on cells and code spans, 7.0 pt type, and pre-wrap for fenced excerpts.
Evidence (all measured on the delivered SHA):
| Check | Result | |---|---| | Cell round-trip vs `manuscript/21-01.md` (de-whitespaced substring, literal `*` preserved) | 3933/3933 cell values visible, 0 missing (`scripts/reader_qa_r35.py`) | | Body words outside the content box / under the footer, all 321 section-21 sheets | 0 | | Vertical single-letter columns (≥4 tight alnum single-letter stack in one x-column) | 0 | | Continuation families tiling `1..N` with truthful ranges | 50/50 families, 0 gaps or inversions | | Whole-artifact sweep, every page | 0 clipped or overlapping words in sections 21 and 24 |
Spot-proofs (vision, this round): `SECTION 21 · SHEET 94` — six columns inside the frame, Storage column wrapped and readable, no footer collision, ten rows 11–20 of 64 visible.

### R35-V02 (BLOCKING) — operation contracts flow, never clip `render_book.split_opcard_fences` now splits any contract fence taller than a sheet at raw line boundaries into measured units of 52 source lines, each printed with the operation ID, the source identifier (`<op> resolved contract (contracts/openapi.yaml via scripts/project_wire.py)`) and an exact line range — `LINES 53–104 OF 1843 · CONTINUED ON NEXT UNIT`, ending `END OF EXCERPT`. Fixed-height clipping is impossible: no unit exceeds the body band, and no `pre` container has a height limit. Provenance is unchanged (the fence bytes are copied, not re-serialised).
| Check | Result | |---|---| | Section-24 sheets rendered | 2112 | | Contracts round-tripped from the printed monospaced spans vs canonical opcard fences | 59/59 byte-identical (de-whitespaced) | | Canonical fences parsing as the same JSON | 59/59 | | `END OF EXCERPT` tail units | 59 (one per contract) | | Body words outside the content box / under the footer | 0 of 2112 sheets |
Spot-proof: `SECTION 24 · SHEET 3` — placard `OP-033, OP-034 · … · LINES 53–104 OF 1843 · CONTINUED ON NEXT UNIT`; coherent middle fragment, ends far above the footer.

### R35-V06 (BLOCKING) — lifecycle model complete and reconciled with its projections The canonical model (`tables/lifecycle-35.json`) is complete: AS-09 `rework→active`, AS-10 `blocked→active`, AS-11 `proposed→withdrawn`, OB-13 `rework→decomposing`, OB-14 `blocked→decomposing`, OB-15/OB-16 `decomposing→cancelled|withdrawn`. All six machines pass reachability, terminal reachability and no-dead-end checks; figures 25.1-1 … 25.6-1 carry exactly the canonical transition IDs (SVG label parity), and tables 25.1-1 … 25.1-6 print all 50 transitions with guards and ordered writes. The recovery law (same-record recovery with explicit `SuccessorLink`, authorized cancellation/withdrawal, original-goal accounting) is published in §25 and §B. This round added the missing **acceptance fixtures** — `tables/lifecycle-35-acceptance.csv` now carries `rework_recovery`, `blocked_release`, `cancellation`, `withdrawn_reachability` and `original_goal_accounting` — plus a restored validator (`scripts/lifecycle-35-validate.py`).
Owner-required traces, each verified legal edge-by-edge against the published model:
| Trace | Legal chain | |---|---| | Rejected work corrected and accepted | active —AS-06→ rework —AS-09→ active —AS-03→ accepted | | Blocked released by a valid replacement | active —AS-07→ blocked —AS-10→ active —AS-03→ accepted | | Objective rework recovery | in_acceptance —OB-11→ rework —OB-13→ decomposing —OB-02→ in_acceptance —OB-03→ accepted | | Objective blocked recovery | decomposing —OB-12→ blocked —OB-14→ decomposing —OB-02→ in_acceptance —OB-03→ accepted | | Authorized cancellation | assigned —AS-08→ cancelled | | Authorized withdrawal | proposed —AS-11→ withdrawn | | Objective cancellation / withdrawal | decomposing —OB-15→ cancelled · decomposing —OB-16→ withdrawn |
Unresolved outcomes remain explicit release gates (`OPEN G-04` native allocation, `G-06` trusted stop-proof producer, `G-12` storage binding); nothing here claims runtime implementation.

### R35-V19 (BLOCKING) — the delivery gate now reads the artifact `scripts/reader_qa_r35.py` is a separate rendered-artifact gate keyed to the delivered PDF hash. It checks source cell values, per-contract tails, placard range continuity, reachability/traces and the `SPEC V3.5` + doc-id stamp on every page; it fails closed and writes `evidence/reader-qa-r35.json`. `scripts/render_audit_all_pages.py` sweeps all 3247 pages for text outside the content box, under the footer, or overlapping. `scripts/qa_final.py` no longer asserts a frozen page count (reference continuation changes the total by design); stamps, doc id, folios, Mermaid and index are still gated. Stale hard-coded section-25 figure page numbers in `reader_qa_deterministic.py` / `reader_qa_span_overlap.py` now resolve captions, so they keep pointing at the right plates after repagination.

## Residual limitations (not claimed fixed or out of this round's scope)
- Whole-artifact sweep finds **13 pre-existing clipped pages outside sections 21/24** (folios 4-19, 10-15, 10-17 … 10-19, 13-6, 17-32, 17-37, 17-61, 17-62, 18-25, 22-18, 23-8). The severe ones are section-17 tables with the same single-letter-column class of defect (17-37, 17-61, 17-62). They belong to their sections' owners; this round was scoped to the R35 V01/V02/V06 surfaces and instructed not to alter other sections' content. - Block-level overlap on section-25 figure plates is the known stroke+fill doubled glyph rendering; the span-level dedupe check (`reader_qa_span_overlap.py`) reports **none** on all seven plates. - `scripts/check_authoring.py` now passes its edition and manuscript checks, then stops at `table-caption: TABLE 26.1-1`: `BOOK.yaml`'s `tables` array predates the current caption regeneration (`register/table-register.json` is the current registry). The offline authoring gate therefore remains red on stale registry data, not on content; its previous PASS receipt was removed from `evidence/gate-receipts.json` because it cannot be reproduced against this tree. The rendered-artifact gates (`reader_qa_r35.py`, `qa_final.py`, `render_audit_all_pages.py`) and the lifecycle validator all pass standalone. - `README.md` and `evidence/lifecycle-author.md` still reference `scripts/lifecycle-35-generate.py`, which does not exist in the tree; the projection generator actually used is `scripts/lifecycle_publish.py` (figures + §25 tables) plus `build_author_manifest.py` (manuscript). The validator command is restored, the generator reference is stale. - `CHD-3.5-complete-print.pdf` is a 94 % scaled copy; it inherits navigation but its text is vector- scaled, so the reader-artifact text checks are keyed to the navigable artifact.

## Prior round (CHD-3.5 V05 round, superseded artifact `2c2badf1…`, 1378 pp)
Blocker closed first: `scripts/lifecycle_publish.py` build error `figure caption for logical_send not matched (0)` — the dead agent's partial run had left TWO figcaption lines per figure, and the caption regex expected an alt-text it no longer matched. The replacement is now idempotent (consumes N existing figcaptions + optional old paragraph, emits exactly one) and runs clean twice consecutively.
Structural rebuild: layout switched from horizontal (layer → x) to vertical top-to-bottom flow, matching state-graph semantics; backward edges no longer run through intermediate state boxes; edge labels placed by rectangle-collision rejection (candidates: t along edge × dy × side; must not touch node boxes or placed labels). Result: zero span-level glyph-box overlaps on all seven section-25 figure pages (was 13 block overlaps, incl. label-on-label collisions such as AS-04/AS-05 and OB-12/OB-14). Entry arrow enters the initial state from above; self-loop clearance widened.
QA method note (honest limitation, prior round): the vision route was unavailable for that whole session (provider transport 503 / 429 quota), so visual adjudication was performed with deterministic geometry checks instead of a human-eye pass. This round vision worked for two spot-proofs (21-94, 24-03) and deterministic checks carry the rest.

## Status
- NOT YET BUILDABLE stamp retained. Specified ≠ fixture-validated ≠ runtime-verified ≠ owner-accepted; native allocation, stop-proof and storage capabilities stay OPEN. - R35-V01, R35-V02 and R35-V06 are closed with the evidence above, keyed to SHA `5c8de616…`; R35-V05 / V04 items from the prior round remain as recorded there, and the other R35 findings are untouched by this rebuild.
